built.label: the rule -- the section heading, a session protocol and a standing rule
built.text: ## SESSION PROTOCOL — reviewer mirror-refresh (standing rule, 2026-07-29)

built.label: the rule -- clause one, any session reasoning about paper CONTENT
built.text: **Any session in which the chat reviewer reasons about paper *content* begins with a fresh mirror-refresh export.** Do not let a reviewer cite versions, statuses, or work-order states from memory or from a prior conversation's mirror — regenerate first.

built.label: the rule -- the procedure, and the MANIFEST`s two columns as the authority
built.text: - **Procedure.** Create `D:\MY-DOwnloads\mirror-refresh-<today>\` fresh; copy in flat the reviewer set (FINDINGS, REGISTRY, OPEN_TRAILS, SPIRAL_MAP, VERIFICATION_LOOM, ERRATA; the five RH-rail papers at current version; EXCLUSION_ENGINE, FOUNDATIONS_OF_THE_SIDE_PROGRAMME, ADDITIVE_MULTIPLICATIVE_CONSPIRACY, BALANCE_AND_POSITIVITY, GRH_CASCADE, SILENCE_STAGES_DEALIGNMENT, FORMATION_DISTANCE_AND_SILENCE_AS_PROTECTION, INVARIANCE_BARRIERS [was SIEVE_CEILING_LEMMA]). Write MANIFEST.md (per file: bytes · md5 · version line · last-commit; header pins the source HEAD; a generated export artifact, not a repo file). Zip. The MANIFEST's md5 + last-commit columns are the reviewer's authority — cite from the export, not from recall.

built.label: the rule -- why it is a hard rule: two recorded errors
built.text: - **Why this is a hard rule, not a nicety.** Stale mirror content has already produced two recorded errors: (1) a **wrong citation** — SURROUND and the REGISTRY `1.5a-5` row cited *Paths to the Critical Line* **v0.2** while the file was at **v0.6** (rowgen constellation caught it; fixed under the `11db565` rail-baseline break); (2) a **wrong work-order status** — W-ORD-C7-WITNESS reported **open** when it had already been **compiled** (closed-by-compile as `Voice7Witness.hadamard_does_not_enforce_online`). Both trace to a reviewer reasoning off a stale snapshot. The refresh closes that class of error at the top of the session.

built.label: the rule -- the currency check, the MANIFEST wins
built.text: - **Currency check.** If a reviewer's claim disagrees with the current MANIFEST (version, md5, or last-commit), the MANIFEST wins and the claim is stale — re-derive before acting on it. Rule 5 above applies transitively: the freshest export wins.

built.label: the standard -- TIER K may be cited as certification
built.text: **Tier K — Keystone-certified.** A document whose load-bearing claims are backed by a **machine-checked kernel terminal at a pin**, Gate-1-graded (DERIVES, or INTERFACES-with-a-named-premise). *Obligation:* every such claim states its **grade · terminal · pin**, and the axiom profile is written in full ("the standard three axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}", or cleaner). *Citation rule:* **may be cited as certification** — the terminal, at its grade, is the warrant.

built.label: the standard -- TIER C is never cited as certification
built.text: **Tier C — Cluster-synthesis.** A document that **organizes** certified results into a cross-system picture, panel, map, or interpretation — asserting *relationships* not individually certified. *Obligation:* state the invariant it organizes on; flag any tuple/value that is a **coordinate, not an invariant**; carry the Gate-1b discipline (classification × certification is the invariant, not a shared tuple). *Citation rule:* **cite for orientation and organization — NEVER as certification of the relationships it draws.** This is the taxonomy's load-bearing rule.

built.label: the standard -- the failure the tiers exist to prevent
built.text: The formation-universality over-claim (June 2026) happened because a **Tier-C synthesis panel** (CATALOGOS's cross-system formation table, assigning (2,3,2,0) to Shannon/Maxwell/DNA) was read and cited **as a Tier-K certification**. The tuple was a synthesis *coordinate*; it was cited as a *proven invariant*. The three-tier taxonomy makes the recurrence impossible by rule: **Tier-C content can never again be read as certification.** A cross-system panel organizes; it does not prove the relationships it tabulates — only the Tier-K terminals it points to are certified, each at its own grade. The parsing-invariant observable (classification × certification) is the only thing a Tier-C panel may assert as holding across its rows.

built.label: the standard -- the two failures it makes structurally impossible
built.text: *Standing standard, 2026-07-28 (Tier E added 2026-08-08, author-ruled). Every corpus document belongs to one of four tiers, and the tier fixes what it must carry and how it may be cited. The taxonomy exists to make two failures structurally impossible: a synthesis being read as a certification, and a filing-facing framing being read as the record. Nothing deposits.*

built.label: the standard -- CATALOGOS, read the panels as C and the terminals as K
built.text: - **CATALOGOS** — a Tier-C synthesis that *contains* Tier-K terminal citations (the Lean-verified counts). It is **Tier C** (its cross-system claims are synthesis), but its individually-pinned terminal rows are K-grade. Read the panels as C, the pinned terminals as K.

built.label: the standard -- UNIVERSALITY, mostly K with the C-scope note
built.text: - **UNIVERSALITY.md** — its ζ_K count-7 claim is K-grade (theorem-supported at the arithmetic tier); its head-note is the Gate-1b C-discipline. **Mostly K, with the C-scope note.**

built.label: the standard -- THE_SUBSTRATE, Tier K containing a Related Work section
built.text: - **THE_SUBSTRATE** — **Tier K** (its Correspondence table is pinned terminals), *containing* a Related Work section (classical citations, not claims). Read as K.

built.label: the standard -- Tier E relaxes the audience, never the certificate
built.text: **Tier E — Filing-facing.** A document written for counsel or a patent examiner rather than for a referee: invention disclosures, per-filing packages and claim-support charts, prior-art and enablement material, and the engineering notes held with them. *Obligation:* mark the attorney-facing grade on its face; carry the **sequencing law** (provisioning precedes publishing and partnering) and, wherever it reconstructs claim content, the **executor-cannot-read-the-filed-claims** caveat; every technical claim still states its **grade · terminal · pin**, exactly as Tier K requires — Tier E relaxes the audience, never the certificate. *Citation rule:* **never cited in a reader-facing paper** — Tier E sits outside the publication line, and a Tier-E document's framing of a result is drafted for claim scope, not for the record. **Tier E cites Tier K; nothing cites Tier E.**
